recentItems.title: Bronx News Today: Fire victims remain displaced, robbery and stabbing suspects wanted
recentItems.description:
A car flipped over on Bronx Park South near East 180th Street late Wednesday night with no reported injuries. Meanwhile, families displaced by the August 21 fire at a Trinity Avenue building in Melrose remain under a vacate order as repairs are planned. NYPD also announced the arrest of Kenneth Godfrey in connection with an August 4 shooting near Westchester and Longwood avenues, while investigators continue searching for suspects tied to a Jerome Avenue stabbing, two delivery driver robberies in Edenwald, and a series of chain snatchings across Fordham, Tremont, Concourse Village, Belmont and West Farms.

recentItems.title: Street fight escalates to armed standoff as suspect barricades inside home
recentItems.description:
An early morning street fight in Bridgeport, Connecticut escalated into an armed standoff after police say a man with a gun fled officers and barricaded himself inside a home. Authorities say Roberto Martins fired at police, prompting at least one officer to return fire, though no one was injured. The 53-year-old suspect later surrendered peacefully with the assistance of a hostage negotiator and now faces multiple charges.

recentItems.title: ICE arrest attempt ends in crash after driver flees
recentItems.description:
An early morning crash on Route 130 in North Brunswick is being linked to an attempted arrest by ICE agents, according to township officials. Authorities say the driver of a gold Acura sped away from ICE, ran a red light and crashed into a Tesla driven by Dr. Penelope Cohen, the wife of East Brunswick Mayor Brad Cohen. The driver allegedly fled the scene before being captured, arrested and taken to a hospital for treatment.

recentItems.title: Chain-snatching crew on mopeds linked to 20+ NYC robberies
recentItems.description:
Police say a group of men riding mopeds has carried out more than 20 chain-snatching robberies across Manhattan and the Bronx since late June. Investigators say the suspects approach victims on the street, rip chains from their necks, and quickly flee. In one recent case, a 27-year-old woman suffered injuries during a struggle before her gold chain was stolen. Police are urging residents to remain alert as the search continues.

recentItems.title: NYC bans AI for public school students through 8th grade
recentItems.description:
More than half a million New York City public school students will be affected by new rules banning generative AI in grades 2-K through 8. Chatbots including ChatGPT, Google Gemini and Claude are prohibited, while high school AI use will be limited to a supervised pilot program. The city says the policy is designed to protect children and preserve student-teacher interaction as schools head back to class.
